standard_prerequisites.name: The perpendicular B(x) of the image of the evaluation map consists of the linear forms vanishing on the images of all R-linear maps, and the quotient V(x) = M(x)/B(x) is the fibre that detects independence
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the objects in terms of which both directions of the equivalence are formulated.

core_obligations: Define B(x) as the perpendicular of the image of the evaluation map from Hom_R(M, R) to Hom over kappa(x) of M(x) with kappa(x), and set V(x) = M(x)/B(x); record that every R-linear map M -> R induces a map V(x) -> kappa(x) and conversely that every kappa(x)-linear map of V(x) arises that way (proof lines 38749-38756).

Prove the forward direction: if s_1, ..., s_r map to linearly independent elements of V(x), choose maps phi_i with phi_i(s_j) congruent to the Kronecker delta modulo the perpendicular, so that the composite R^r -> M -> R^r has a determinant f mapping to 1 in kappa(x), whence f does not lie in x and the tuple is the inclusion of a direct summand after inverting f (proof lines 38759-38772).

Prove the converse: if the tuple becomes the inclusion of a direct summand after inverting some f not in x, choose R_f-linear maps phi_i with phi_i(s_j) = delta_ij in R_f, use that Hom from a finitely presented module commutes with localization to clear denominators, and obtain maps phi'_i over R with phi'_i(s_j) = f^n delta_ij (proof lines 38774-38783).

Conclude that the images of s_1, ..., s_r in V(x) are linearly independent, since the induced maps satisfy the displayed relation with the unit f^n, which completes the equivalence (proof lines 38783-38785).
proof_roadmap: Introduce the perpendicular B(x) of the evaluation image and the quotient V(x), and record the duality between maps M -> R and maps V(x) -> kappa(x) (proof lines 38748-38756).
From independence in V(x), build a dual family whose composite with the tuple has determinant not in x, giving the splitting after inverting that determinant (proof lines 38758-38772).

From a splitting after inverting f, produce dual maps over R_f, clear denominators using localization of Hom from a finitely presented module, and read off the independence in V(x) (proof lines 38774-38785).
difficulty_reason: The statement compares two conditions for a tuple s_1, ..., s_r of elements of a module M in a fixed situation over a scheme: that the tuple becomes the inclusion of a direct summand after inverting some element f outside a point x, and that the images of the tuple in the fibre V(x) are linearly independent (statement lines 38730-38746). The proof introduces a perpendicular B(x) inside the fibre M(x) together with its quotient V(x), shows that the evaluation maps realise all linear forms on V(x), and then runs the two directions: independence in V(x) produces a dual family whose composite with the tuple has a determinant outside x, while a splitting after inverting f is turned into dual maps over R by clearing denominators through the localization behaviour of Hom from a finitely presented module (proof lines 38749-38785). The subtle point is the passage from maps over the localization back to maps over R, which is what makes the equivalence canonical.
